question.prompt:
A rectangular board of \(8\) columns has squares numbered beginning in the upper left corner and moving left to right so row one is numbered \(1\) through \(8,\) row two is \(9\) through \(16,\) and so on. A student shades square \(1,\) then skips one square and shades square \(3,\) skips two squares and shades square \(6,\) skips \(3\) squares and shades square \(10,\) and continues in this way until there is at least one shaded square in each column.

What is the number of the shaded square that first achieves this result?

[Figure 1](figures/1998_AMC_8_Q24_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Each row contains eight squares, so dividing a square's number by \(8\) identifies its column: remainders \(1\) through \(7\) give those columns, and remainder \(0\) means column \(8\). For example, \(21=2\cdot8+5\), so square \(21\) is in column \(5\).

Skipping one square moves forward two squares, skipping two moves forward three, and so on. Thus we generate the shaded numbers by adding \(2,3,4,\ldots\) successively. The first seven shaded numbers are
\[
1,3,6,10,15,21,28.
\]
Their columns, in the same order, are
\[
1,3,6,2,7,5,4.
\]
Every column except column \(8\) has now been reached. To find when that last column is reached, continue adding \(8,9,\ldots\). The next shaded numbers are
\[
36,45,55,66,78,91,105,120,
\]
and their columns are respectively
\[
4,5,7,2,6,3,1,8.
\]
These lists include every shading step up to \(120\). Column \(8\) appears for the first time at \(120\), when all other columns have already appeared. Therefore the answer is \(\boxed{120}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Track shaded numbers and their columns
